subject: EU consent & tracking: telemetry, cookies, and data transfer questions
messages:
From: Sarah Long <sarah.long@acme-corp.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: EU consent, tracking, and transfers — telemetry questions

Hi Laura,

Our privacy team asked me to confirm a few specifics about how Redwood handles console telemetry and website/marketing analytics before we proceed with a pilot in the EU. Short list:

- Does Redwood's telemetry (console usage, error traces, feature flags) ever collect PII (names, email addresses, full IPs) by default?
- Which cookies does the Redwood Console set for logged-in users vs. end-customer websites (marketing analytics)? First- or third-party?
- Where are telemetry logs and analytics stored (region)? Are they transferred to the US?
- Can you provide your current DPA + subprocessors list and confirm whether SCCs or the EU Data Privacy Framework are used?
- Is there a supported config to keep marketing analytics strictly off until we have consent (cookie banner integration / minimal mode)?

I attached a short diagram of our desired flow (product-telemetry-flows.pdf). Our legal team would like to see subprocessors and the DPA before signing. Can you point me to the right contact and timeline?

Thanks,
Sarah Long
Privacy Program Manager — Acme Corp
Attachment: product-telemetry-flows.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: EU consent, tracking, and transfers — telemetry questions

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list and the diagram. Looping in David (legal) and Ava (product) so we can give you concise, actionable answers and the paperwork. Quick summary up front:

- Telemetry defaults: console telemetry is designed to collect non-identifying telemetry (events, aggregated metrics, anonymized session IDs). We do not capture user-entered content or account PII by default.
- Optional traces: there is an opt-in feature for session-level traces which may capture identifiers for debugging; this is disabled by default and requires org-level consent.
- Cookies: the Redwood Console uses first-party session cookies for authentication and UX. Our hosted website/marketing analytics can be configured either as third-party analytics (default for quick installs) or as first-party via our cookieless/consent-mode integration.
- Storage & transfers: hosted telemetry and analytics are stored in US regions for the hosted product. We have an EU-region offering for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- DPA & subprocessors: we have a standard DPA and publish our subprocessors list; legal can send you the DPA link and the signed SCCs we currently use.

Next steps I propose:
1) David — can you drop the DPA + subprocessors list and any standard SCC/Sample clause?
2) Ava — can you share the product doc that shows how to set analytics to "minimal"/consent-first and how to enable EU-storage or Dedicated?
3) Sarah — if you can share any must-have contract language or timeline (and confirm who on your side will review DPA), we'll prioritize.

I've attached a short overview image that might help. Happy to set a 30-min call this week.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah / Laura / Ava,

Thanks — quick legal response and links below. I'll keep this high level and attach the formal docs.

Key points:
- PII & telemetry: Redwood's hosted telemetry pipeline is configured to avoid collection of account-level PII by default. Where identifiers are used (session id, anonymized user id), we recommend pseudonymization. If you require zero identifiers, we offer a "minimal telemetry" profile that turns off session-level metrics and only collects aggregate counts.
- Cookies & consent: Marketing analytics (website) are considered marketing/analytics cookies under Art. 4 GDPR guidance; you should obtain active consent for non-essential cookies. We support integration with common consent managers (OneTrust, Cookiebot) and provide a consent-mode API so analytics are paused until consent is granted. For the Console, first-party session cookies are necessary for auth; those are legitimate interest (essential) but we can scope retention.
- Data transfers / DPA: Our standard DPA is at https://redwood-inference.com/legal/dpa; we currently implement EU SCCs for hosted accounts and are tracking guidance for the EU-US Data Privacy Framework. We can execute SCCs and add a data localization addendum for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Subprocessors: see attached list (subprocessors-2026-03.pdf). High-level examples: AWS (EC2, S3), Google Cloud (BigQuery), Cloudflare, Datadog, Sentry, Segment/RudderStack (optional depending on integration). If you have specific vendor exclusions, let us know and we can assess.
- Security controls: encryption at rest (KMS), TLS in transit, role-based access controls, logging/audit trails. We can offer retention-limited access to telemetry for debugging and purge logs on request subject to the SLA.

If Acme needs to redline any DPA provisions, please send the redlines to privacy@redwood-inference.com and we will route them to our contracts team. For an accelerated timeline, we can provide the subprocessors PDF and a DocuSign DPA link (placeholder below).

Attachments: subprocessors-2026-03.pdf (application/pdf)
Links: https://redwood-inference.com/legal/dpa ; https://redwood-inference.com/subprocessors/2026/ ; https://docusign.com/some-placeholder-dpa

Happy to jump on the call if you want clause-by-clause review.

Regards,
David Kim
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
